question: Which component executes program instructions? A) Monitor B) CPU C) Keyboard D) Printer
reference_explanation: The CPU executes program instructions and performs processing operations.

question: Which type of memory is normally volatile? A) SSD B) RAM C) ROM D) DVD
reference_explanation: RAM normally loses its stored contents when power is removed.

question: What is a main role of an operating system? A) Manufacture hardware B) Design websites only C) Manage system resources D) Replace the CPU
reference_explanation: An operating system manages resources such as processes, memory, and devices.

question: Which digits are used in the binary number system? A) 0 and 1 B) 0 through 7 C) 0 through 9 D) 1 through 10
reference_explanation: Binary is a base-two number system that uses only the digits 0 and 1.

question: Which protocol is commonly used to transfer web pages? A) SMTP B) HTTP C) FTP only D) BIOS
reference_explanation: HTTP is a protocol used for communication between web clients and servers.

question: What does DNS commonly translate into an IP address? A) A file size B) A password C) A domain name D) A CPU instruction
reference_explanation: DNS resolves domain names to corresponding IP addresses and other DNS records.

question: What is a primary key used for in a relational database? A) Encrypt every table B) Uniquely identify a row C) Make every value identical D) Delete backups
reference_explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table.

question: Which SQL command is used to retrieve data? A) SELECT B) DROP C) UPDATE only D) FORMAT
reference_explanation: SELECT retrieves data from one or more database tables or views.

question: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search in an unsorted list of n items? A) O(1) B) O(log n) C) O(n) D) O(n squared)
reference_explanation: Linear search may inspect all n items, giving O(n) worst-case time.

question: Which data structure follows Last In, First Out (LIFO)? A) Queue B) Stack C) Graph D) Tree
reference_explanation: A stack removes the most recently added item first.

question: Which data structure normally follows First In, First Out (FIFO)? A) Queue B) Stack C) Heap only D) Recursion
reference_explanation: A queue normally removes items in the same order they were added.

question: What is recursion? A) Deleting a variable B) Sorting without comparisons C) A function calling itself D) Turning off a computer
reference_explanation: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself directly or indirectly.

question: What does a traditional ahead-of-time compiler generally do? A) Clean the keyboard B) Translate source code into a target form before execution C) Increase RAM physically D) Assign IP addresses
reference_explanation: A compiler translates source code into another form, often machine code, before execution.

question: What is Git mainly used for? A) Version control B) Image compression only C) Power management D) Database hosting only
reference_explanation: Git tracks changes to files and supports collaborative version control.

question: Which security property does encryption primarily help protect? A) Screen brightness B) CPU temperature C) Confidentiality D) Keyboard layout
reference_explanation: Encryption helps keep information confidential by making it unreadable without the appropriate key.

question: How should a system normally store user passwords for verification? A) Store salted password hashes B) Save every password in plain text C) Put passwords in a public file D) Email passwords to all users
reference_explanation: Passwords should be stored using an appropriate password-hashing algorithm with a unique salt.

question: What is phishing? A) A database backup method B) A deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information C) A sorting algorithm D) A type of RAM
reference_explanation: Phishing uses deceptive messages or sites to trick people into revealing information or taking unsafe actions.

question: What does a firewall commonly do? A) Compile programs B) Replace a database C) Filter network traffic according to rules D) Increase monitor resolution
reference_explanation: A firewall permits or blocks network traffic according to configured security rules.

question: What does an IP address help identify? A) A program's source code B) A network interface or endpoint C) A computer's screen size D) A database password
reference_explanation: An IP address identifies a network interface or endpoint for Internet Protocol communication.

question: Which transport protocol provides reliable, ordered delivery of a byte stream? A) TCP B) UDP C) ARP D) DNS
reference_explanation: TCP provides reliable, ordered byte-stream delivery.

question: Which statement about UDP is correct? A) It guarantees delivery B) It always retransmits lost packets C) It does not guarantee delivery or ordering D) It is a database query language
reference_explanation: UDP does not guarantee packet delivery, retransmission, or ordering.

question: What is a loop commonly used for? A) Physically adding memory B) Repeating a block of instructions C) Encrypting every file automatically D) Replacing an operating system
reference_explanation: A loop repeats a block of instructions while its iteration conditions allow it.

question: Why are functions useful? A) They package reusable behavior B) They always remove all bugs C) They replace all variables D) They make programs need no testing
reference_explanation: Functions organize behavior into reusable units and can reduce duplicated code.

question: In Python, which construct is commonly used to handle exceptions? A) SELECT FROM B) HTML BODY C) try and except D) IP and DNS
reference_explanation: Python uses try and except blocks to catch and handle exceptions.

question: What is one major goal of database normalization? A) Increase duplicate data B) Reduce unnecessary redundancy C) Remove all keys D) Turn tables into images
reference_explanation: Normalization organizes relational data to reduce undesirable redundancy and update anomalies.

question: What is an API commonly used for? A) Allowing software components to communicate B) Cleaning physical hardware C) Replacing every algorithm D) Measuring monitor size
reference_explanation: An API defines how software components can request services or exchange information.

question: What is the main purpose of a cache? A) Permanently replace all storage B) Generate passwords C) Keep frequently needed data available for faster access D) Remove the operating system
reference_explanation: A cache stores copies of useful data to reduce access time.

question: What is overfitting in machine learning? A) A model cannot be stored B) A model fits training data well but generalizes poorly to unseen data C) A model has no parameters D) A dataset contains only integers
reference_explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns training-specific patterns and performs poorly on new data.

question: Why is a held-out test dataset used? A) To estimate performance on unseen data B) To train on every test answer repeatedly C) To replace the training process D) To increase the file size
reference_explanation: A held-out test set estimates how well a model generalizes to data not used for training.

question: What is two-factor authentication (2FA)? A) Using the same password twice B) Having two usernames C) Using two different authentication factors D) Logging in without authentication
reference_explanation: Two-factor authentication requires evidence from two different factor categories.
